past.name: Software Internals Meetup #1 - Redis & Kubernetes

event_locations.name: Essentia.dev
event_locations.address: Third Floor, C56/A28, C Block, Phase 2, Industrial Area, Sector 62, Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201309

past.description:
PyDelhi Software Internals Meetup #1

A new PyDelhi format for going deeper into how the systems we work with actually work under the hood.

This is not a beginner-friendly talk meetup. We’re keeping the group intentionally small and the discussions intentionally technical: 15 seats only, for software professionals with 1+ year of industry experience.

Expect detailed walkthroughs, internals, implementation decisions, and discussion around how these systems work beyond their public APIs.

Talks

The Redis Core: TCP, RESP & Event-Driven I/O

Sagar Deep — SDE 1, Essentia.dev

Redis is often treated as a black box: send a command, get a response. In this session, Sagar will go deeper into what actually happens inside Redis.

We’ll look at the foundations of Redis, including:

  • How Redis communicates over TCP

  • How the RESP protocol works

  • How Redis handles connections and requests

  • Event-driven I/O and the event loop

  • How these pieces come together to power Redis' performance

From kubectl apply to Reconciliation: Inside the Kubernetes API Machinery

Ghanatava — Freelance DevOps Engineer

What actually happens after you run kubectl apply?

This session will trace the request through Kubernetes' API machinery and into the reconciliation model that drives the cluster.

We’ll dig into:

  • What happens inside the Kubernetes API server

  • How API requests are processed

  • Object storage and the path to etcd

  • Watches, controllers, and reconciliation

  • How Kubernetes turns a declarative request into actual cluster state

Format

This will be a deep-study and discussion-style meetup, rather than a typical conference-style event.

There will be time to pause, ask questions, discuss implementation details, and explore the parts of the systems that usually get abstracted away.

15 seats only.

Eligibility: 1+ years of professional software engineering experience.

past.description:
PyDelhi Security BOF (Birds of a Feather)

Join the PyDelhi community for an open, informal gathering focused on Python security — one of the most critical and fast-evolving areas in software development today.

A Birds of a Feather (BOF) session is an informal, discussion-driven meetup where participants with shared interests come together to exchange ideas, experiences, and knowledge. There are no keynotes or rigid agendas — just passionate people talking about what they know and care about.

What to Expect

This session will bring together developers, security researchers, ethical hackers, and Python enthusiasts to discuss topics such as:

  • Secure coding practices in Python
  • Common vulnerabilities in Python applications (OWASP Top 10 and beyond)
  • Tools for static analysis, fuzzing, and penetration testing (e.g., Bandit, PyRDP, Scapy)
  • Dependency security and supply chain risks
  • CTF challenges and war stories from the field
  • Building security-aware Python communities

Who Should Attend

This meetup is open to everyone — whether you are a seasoned security professional, a developer curious about hardening your Python code, or a student just getting started with application security. All skill levels are welcome.

past.description:
🐍 PyDelhi October Meetup — Birds of a Feather (BoF)

For working professionals only

What happens when you bring a group of Pythonistas together on a Saturday afternoon?
You get a lively nest of opinionated ideas that fuel freely-flowing (almost slithering) conversations.

PyDelhi and PyData Delhi is back with the October edition of our monthly meetups, this time in a Birds of a Feather (BoF) format!

🤔 What’s a BoF?

While there’s no formal definition (and strangely no Wikipedia page), a loose one would be:

"It is an informal gathering where people come to discuss pre-decided (and sometimes on-the-spot) topics and talk about their experiences, stories and learnings with said topic."

We’ll have multiple topics running in parallel for the BoFs.

📌 Who should join?

This edition is exclusively for working professionals with significant experience in Python, engineering and/or open source.

If that’s you, feel free to suggest a topic of your choice or lead one of the sessions listed below:

  • Python in Production — scaling from prototype to prod, debugging, deployment hacks
  • Async & Concurrency — real-world wins and gotchas with asyncio, Trio, async frameworks
  • Scaling APIs & Services — FastAPI/Django/Flask in high-traffic, perf tricks, cloud-native issues
  • Tooling & Best Practices — mypy, pyright, pytest, packaging pains, productivity hacks
  • Data & ML in Python — running ML pipelines, MLOps tooling, going beyond notebooks
  • Python + Rust/C Extensions — mixing langs for performance, PyO3, Cython, Numba lessons
  • Testing at Scale — contract testing, property-based, pytest tricks in big teams
  • Engineering Culture — mentoring, reviews, Python team culture, career growth
  • Security & Supply Chain — PyPI issues, vendoring, SBOMs, reproducible builds, dependency hell
  • Open Source in the Enterprise — adopting OSS tools internally, leadership buy-in, migrations
